text: I photographed the deer with a long lens.
ir: (assert (e1 photograph :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 deer :det the) :obl-with (m3 lens :det a :adj long)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): 'with a long lens' attaches to the verb (instrument). Reading 2: attaches to 'deer' (the deer that has a long lens).

text: Maria watched the children with the binoculars.
ir: (assert (e1 watch :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :obj (m2 child :det the :num pl) :obl-with (m3 binocular :det the :num pl)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): Maria used the binoculars (verb attachment). Reading 2: the children who had the binoculars (:obl-with on m2). Head 'binocular' singular lemma of plurale tantum.

text: We discussed the problem with the landlord.
ir: (assert (e1 discuss :tense past :subj (m1 we :pron) :obj (m2 problem :det the) :obl-with (m3 landlord :det the)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): discussed it together with the landlord (verb attachment). Reading 2: the problem with (= concerning) the landlord (:obl-with on m2).

text: The police stopped the driver with the broken taillight.
ir: (assert (e1 stop :tense past :subj (m1 police :det the) :obj (m2 driver :det the :obl-with (m3 taillight :det the :adj broken))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the driver whose car has the broken taillight (noun attachment). Reading 2: the police used the broken taillight to stop him (verb attachment, odd but grammatical). 'police' treated as singular-form head without :num.

text: I met the sister of the doctor who lives in Boston.
ir: (assert (e1 meet :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 sister :det the :obl-of (m3 doctor :det the :rel (e2 live :tense pres :subj m3 :obl-in (m4 Boston :propn))))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the doctor lives in Boston (relative clause on m3). Reading 2: the sister lives in Boston (relative clause on m2, gap m2).

text: Sam ordered the cake for the party on Saturday.
ir: (assert (e1 order :tense past :subj (m1 Sam :propn) :obj (m2 cake :det the :obl-for (m3 party :det the :obl-on (m4 Saturday :propn)))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the party is on Saturday (:obl-on on m3). Reading 2: Sam placed the order on Saturday (:obl-on on e1). Also possible: 'for the party' on the verb. Weekday annotated :propn.

text: Robin said that the package arrived yesterday.
ir: (assert (e1 say :tense past :subj (m1 Robin :propn) :comp (e2 arrive :tense past :subj (m2 package :det the) :adv yesterday)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the arrival was yesterday (:adv on e2). Reading 2: the saying was yesterday (:adv on e1).

text: Maria said Tom would call if the train was late.
ir: (assert (e1 say :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :comp (e2 call :mod would :subj (m2 Tom :propn) :condition (e3 be :tense past :subj (m3 train :det the) :attr late))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the condition is part of what was said (:condition on e2). Reading 2: Maria made the statement only if the train was late (:condition on e1).

text: I read the review of the film in the newspaper.
ir: (assert (e1 read :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 review :det the :obl-of (m3 film :det the) :obl-in (m4 newspaper :det the))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the review in the newspaper (:obl-in on m2). Reading 2: the reading happened in the newspaper (:obl-in on e1). Reading 3: the film in the newspaper (:obl-in on m3).

text: Alex cut the bread on the counter.
ir: (assert (e1 cut :tense past :subj (m1 Alex :propn) :obj (m2 bread :det the) :obl-on (m3 counter :det the)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the cutting took place on the counter (verb). Reading 2: the bread that was on the counter (:obl-on on m2).

text: The guide told the tourists that the museum was closed at noon.
ir: (assert (e1 tell :tense past :subj (m1 guide :det the) :iobj (m2 tourist :det the :num pl) :comp (e2 be :tense past :subj (m3 museum :det the) :attr closed :obl-at (m4 noon))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the museum was closed at noon (:obl-at on e2). Reading 2: the telling happened at noon (:obl-at on e1). The first object of 'tell' + that-clause annotated :iobj (spec silent).

text: We need the key to the cabinet in the office.
ir: (assert (e1 need :tense pres :subj (m1 we :pron) :obj (m2 key :det the :obl-to (m3 cabinet :det the :obl-in (m4 office :det the)))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the cabinet is in the office (:obl-in on m3). Reading 2: the key is in the office (:obl-in on m2). Reading 3: the needing is in the office (:obl-in on e1).

text: The nurse checked the patient after the surgery.
ir: (assert (e1 check :tense past :subj (m1 nurse :det the) :obj (m2 patient :det the) :obl-after (m3 surgery :det the)) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the checking happened after the surgery (verb). Reading 2: the patient (who was) after the surgery (:obl-after on m2), i.e. the post-surgery patient.

text: Look at the dog with one eye.
ir: (command (e1 look :subj (m1 you :pron :implicit) :obl-at (m2 dog :det the :obl-with (m3 eye :det one))) :ambig attachment)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): the dog that has one eye (:obl-with on m2). Reading 2: look using one eye (:obl-with on e1).

text: Every guest brought a salad.
ir: (assert (e1 bring :tense past :subj (m1 guest :det every) :obj (m2 salad :det a)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated, IR identical for both): every > a, each guest brought a (possibly different) salad. Reading 2: a > every, one salad that all guests brought. v0 IR does not encode scope, so only the flag differs.

text: A volunteer greeted every visitor.
ir: (assert (e1 greet :tense past :subj (m1 volunteer :det a) :obj (m2 visitor :det every)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: a > every, one volunteer greeted all visitors. Reading 2: every > a, each visitor was greeted by some volunteer. Same IR.

text: Two waiters served three tables.
ir: (assert (e1 serve :tense past :subj (m1 waiter :det two :num pl) :obj (m2 table :det three :num pl)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: cumulative, three tables in total. Reading 2: each of the two waiters served three tables (six in total). Reading 3: three tables each served by two waiters. Same IR.

text: All the guests didn't leave.
ir: (assert (e1 leave :tense past :pol neg :subj (m1 guest :det all :det the :num pl)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: all > not, no guest left. Reading 2: not > all, not every guest left. 'all the' annotated as two :det atoms (spec silent on predeterminers); the checker's rule realizer drops 'the' when rendering this.

text: I didn't leave the party because I was bored.
ir: (assert (e1 leave :tense past :pol neg :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 party :det the) :cause (e2 be :tense past :subj (m3 I :pron) :attr bored)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: because > not, I stayed, and the reason was boredom. Reading 2: not > because, I left, but not because I was bored. Same IR (v0 has no negation-scope marking).

text: Each parent spoke with a teacher.
ir: (assert (e1 speak :tense past :subj (m1 parent :det each) :obl-with (m2 teacher :det a)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: each > a, possibly different teachers. Reading 2: a > each, one particular teacher. Same IR.

text: Someone cleaned every room.
ir: (assert (e1 clean :tense past :subj (m1 someone) :obj (m2 room :det every)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: someone > every, one person cleaned all rooms. Reading 2: every > someone, each room was cleaned by somebody. Same IR.

text: We didn't sell the car because it was old.
ir: (assert (e1 sell :tense past :pol neg :subj (m1 we :pron) :obj (m2 car :det the) :cause (e2 be :tense past :subj (m3 it :pron :ref m2) :attr old)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: because > not, we kept the car because it was old. Reading 2: not > because, we sold it, but not because it was old. 'it' -> car only.

text: Every student in the room speaks two languages.
ir: (assert (e1 speak :tense pres :subj (m1 student :det every :obl-in (m2 room :det the)) :obj (m3 language :det two :num pl)) :ambig scope)
notes: Reading 1: every > two, each student speaks two (maybe different) languages. Reading 2: two > every, there are two languages that every student speaks. Same IR.

text: We walked to the bank.
ir: (assert (e1 walk :tense past :subj (m1 we :pron) :obl-to (m2 bank :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: financial institution. Reading 2: river bank. Same IR.

text: Sam found a bat in the garage.
ir: (assert (e1 find :tense past :subj (m1 Sam :propn) :obj (m2 bat :det a) :obl-in (m3 garage :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: the animal. Reading 2: a club for baseball/cricket. Same IR. (Also a minor attachment ambiguity: 'in the garage' on the verb vs the noun; annotated on the verb.)

text: I left my glasses on the table.
ir: (assert (e1 leave :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 glass :poss (m3 I :pron) :num pl) :obl-on (m4 table :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: spectacles. Reading 2: drinking glasses. Same IR (lemma 'glass' in both; spectacles sense is a plural-only use).

text: Robin forgot the date.
ir: (assert (e1 forget :tense past :subj (m1 Robin :propn) :obj (m2 date :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: the calendar day. Reading 2: a romantic appointment (or the person). Reading 3: the fruit. Same IR.

text: The seal was damaged.
ir: (assert (e1 damage :tense past :voice pass :subj (m1 seal :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: a closure/stamp (e.g. on a jar or document). Reading 2: the marine animal. Same IR. 'was damaged' annotated passive (could also be be + adjective).

text: We could see the crane from the window.
ir: (assert (e1 see :mod could :subj (m1 we :pron) :obj (m2 crane :det the) :obl-from (m3 window :det the)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: construction machine. Reading 2: the bird. Same IR.

text: The match was short.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense past :subj (m1 match :det the) :attr short) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: a sports game. Reading 2: a matchstick. Same IR.

text: The trunk was empty.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense past :subj (m1 trunk :det the) :attr empty) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: the storage space of a car. Reading 2: a large travel chest. (Tree trunk / elephant trunk are less natural with 'empty'.) Same IR.

text: The coach was late.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense past :subj (m1 coach :det the) :attr late) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: the sports trainer. Reading 2: the long-distance bus. Same IR.

text: Maria kept the letters in a box.
ir: (assert (e1 keep :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :obj (m2 letter :det the :num pl) :obl-in (m3 box :det a)) :ambig lexical)
notes: Reading 1: written messages. Reading 2: alphabet letters (e.g. tiles or cut-outs). Same IR.

text: I bought fresh bread and milk.
ir: (assert (e1 buy :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (and (m2 bread :adj fresh) (m3 milk))) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): 'fresh' modifies only 'bread'. Reading 2: 'fresh' modifies both conjuncts (:adj fresh repeated on m3).

text: The old men and women sat near the door.
ir: (assert (e1 sit :tense past :subj (and (m1 man :det the :num pl :adj old) (m2 woman :num pl)) :obl-near (m3 door :det the)) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): only the men are old. Reading 2: both are old (:adj old also on m2). In both readings 'the' arguably distributes over both conjuncts; annotated only on m1 (surface-faithful, spec silent on shared determiners).

text: Maria told the boy that she liked the story.
ir: (assert (e1 tell :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :iobj (m2 boy :det the) :comp (e2 like :tense past :subj (m3 she :pron :ref m1) :obj (m4 story :det the))) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): that-clause is the complement of 'told' (she said she liked the story). Reading 2: 'that she liked' is a relative clause on 'boy' (the boy she liked), and 'the story' is the direct object of 'told': (m2 boy :det the :rel (e2 like :subj (she) :obj m2)) :obj (m4 story). In reading 1 'the boy' is annotated :iobj (spec silent for tell + clause). 'she' -> Maria only.

text: We will eat pasta and drink wine or go home.
ir: (assert (or (and (e1 eat :tense fut :subj (m1 we :pron) :obj (m2 pasta)) (e2 drink :tense fut :subj (m3 we :pron) :obj (m4 wine))) (e3 go :tense fut :subj (m5 we :pron) :adv home)) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): (eat and drink) or go home. Reading 2: eat, and (drink or go home): (and e1 (or e2 e3)). Shared subject 'we' and 'will' repeated on each conjunct (spec silent on ellipsis in clause coordination). 'home' as :adv.

text: The chicken is ready to eat.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense pres :subj (m1 chicken :det the) :attr ready :xcomp (e2 eat)) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1: the chicken will be eaten (object gap). Reading 2: the chicken (animal) is about to eat (subject control). Same IR: v0 cannot mark the gap position. Infinitival complement of an adjective attached as :xcomp on the be-clause (spec silent).

text: I saw her duck.
ir: (assert (e1 see :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 duck :poss (m3 she :pron :ref none))) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): 'her duck' = possessive + noun. Reading 2: 'her' is the object and 'duck' a bare-infinitive verb (I saw her lower her head): (e1 see :obj (m2 she :pron) :xcomp (e2 duck)) - bare-infinitive perception complement not covered by spec. Also lexical (duck noun/verb).

text: Small dogs and cats are welcome in the hotel.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense pres :subj (and (m1 dog :num pl :adj small) (m2 cat :num pl)) :attr welcome :obl-in (m3 hotel :det the)) :ambig structural)
notes: Reading 1 (annotated): only the dogs must be small. Reading 2: small dogs and small cats (:adj small on m2 too). Also attachment: 'in the hotel' could modify the coordination's second noun; annotated on the verb.

text: With a long lens, I photographed the deer.
ir: (assert (e1 photograph :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 deer :det the) :obl-with (m3 lens :det a :adj long)))
notes: Control for t6-001: fronted PP can only modify the clause.

text: Maria watched them with the binoculars.
ir: (assert (e1 watch :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :obj (m2 they :pron :ref none) :obl-with (m3 binocular :det the :num pl)))
notes: Control for t6-002: a pronoun object cannot take a PP modifier, so verb attachment only. 'them' has no plural antecedent: :ref none.

text: I met the sisters of the doctor who lives in Boston.
ir: (assert (e1 meet :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 sister :det the :num pl :obl-of (m3 doctor :det the :rel (e2 live :tense pres :subj m3 :obl-in (m4 Boston :propn))))))
notes: Control for t6-005: singular 'lives' agrees only with 'doctor'.

text: Yesterday Robin said that the package arrived.
ir: (assert (e1 say :tense past :subj (m1 Robin :propn) :adv yesterday :comp (e2 arrive :tense past :subj (m2 package :det the))))
notes: Control for t6-007: fronted 'yesterday' modifies the main clause only.

text: Alex cut it on the counter.
ir: (assert (e1 cut :tense past :subj (m1 Alex :propn) :obj (m2 it :pron :ref none) :obl-on (m3 counter :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-010: a pronoun object cannot take a PP modifier, so verb attachment only. 'it': :ref none. Spec gap: §6 rule 2 only excludes the subject, so read literally 'the counter' (co-argument oblique) would be a candidate; excluded here on standard binding grounds.

text: After the surgery, the nurse checked the patient.
ir: (assert (e1 check :tense past :subj (m1 nurse :det the) :obj (m2 patient :det the) :obl-after (m3 surgery :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-013: fronted PP modifies the clause.

text: Look at the dog that has one eye.
ir: (command (e1 look :subj (m1 you :pron :implicit) :obl-at (m2 dog :det the :rel (e2 have :tense pres :subj m2 :obj (m3 eye :det one)))))
notes: Control for t6-014: relative clause makes the noun attachment explicit.

text: Every guest signed the book.
ir: (assert (e1 sign :tense past :subj (m1 guest :det every) :obj (m2 book :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-015: definite object, no scope interaction.

text: A volunteer greeted the visitors.
ir: (assert (e1 greet :tense past :subj (m1 volunteer :det a) :obj (m2 visitor :det the :num pl)))
notes: Control for t6-016.

text: Two waiters served the table.
ir: (assert (e1 serve :tense past :subj (m1 waiter :det two :num pl) :obj (m2 table :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-017.

text: None of the guests left.
ir: (assert (e1 leave :tense past :subj (m1 none :obl-of (m2 guest :det the :num pl))))
notes: Control for t6-018. 'none' annotated as head with partitive :obl-of and no :pol neg (spec lists only not/n't/never as clause negators).

text: I didn't leave the party, because I was having fun.
ir: (assert (e1 leave :tense past :pol neg :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 party :det the) :cause (e2 have :tense past :aspect prog :subj (m3 I :pron) :obj (m4 fun))))
notes: Control for t6-019: the comma puts the because-clause outside the negation (only 'because > not').

text: Everyone laughed at the joke.
ir: (assert (e1 laugh :tense past :subj (m1 everyone) :obl-at (m2 joke :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-021: single quantifier.

text: We walked to the river bank.
ir: (assert (e1 walk :tense past :subj (m1 we :pron) :obl-to (m2 bank :det the :compound river)))
notes: Control for t6-023: compound 'river' decides the sense.

text: Sam found a baseball bat in the garage.
ir: (assert (e1 find :tense past :subj (m1 Sam :propn) :obj (m2 bat :det a :compound baseball) :obl-in (m3 garage :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-024: compound decides the sense ('in the garage' attachment annotated on the verb as in t6-024).

text: I cleaned the lenses of my glasses.
ir: (assert (e1 clean :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (m2 lens :det the :num pl :obl-of (m3 glass :poss (m4 I :pron) :num pl))))
notes: Control for t6-025: 'lenses' selects the spectacles sense.

text: The bus was late.
ir: (assert (e1 be :tense past :subj (m1 bus :det the) :attr late))
notes: Control for t6-031.

text: I bought fresh bread and fresh milk.
ir: (assert (e1 buy :tense past :subj (m1 I :pron) :obj (and (m2 bread :adj fresh) (m3 milk :adj fresh))))
notes: Control for t6-033: adjective repeated on each conjunct.

text: The old men and the young women sat near the door.
ir: (assert (e1 sit :tense past :subj (and (m1 man :det the :num pl :adj old) (m2 woman :det the :num pl :adj young)) :obl-near (m3 door :det the)))
notes: Control for t6-034: each conjunct has its own determiner and adjective.

text: Maria told the boy that the story was funny.
ir: (assert (e1 tell :tense past :subj (m1 Maria :propn) :iobj (m2 boy :det the) :comp (e2 be :tense past :subj (m3 story :det the) :attr funny)))
notes: Control for t6-035: the that-clause has no gap, so it cannot be a relative clause.
